summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube for management of post-bypass hypoglycemia was admitted to the surgery/bariatric service after symptomatic hypoglycemia at home (BG 43 improved with glucose tablets) and concern for increased painful drainage around the G-tube. Imaging with contrast through the tube confirmed the G-tube was appropriately positioned in the stomach without extraluminal leak, and tube feeds were continued with no hypoglycemic events on hospital day 1. She was restarted on metronidazole for suspected small intestinal bacterial overgrowth potentially contributing to hypoglycemia, and granulation tissue at the tube site was treated with silver nitrate and mupirocin ointment. At the request of her outpatient endocrinologist, she completed an inpatient supervised fasting hypoglycemia evaluation with hourly fingersticks and timed labs (including glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, and ammonia); after ~12 hours off feeds her fingerstick reached 55, labs were drawn, and hypoglycemia was treated. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with glucose readings 55–110 overnight, prescriptions for metronidazole and mupirocin, and instructions to follow up with endocrinology to review the fasting study results and continue tube-site care.
